To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two deglucoteioplanin amides (766 and 934) are taken up by gram-negative bacteria by self-promoted uptake, which involves binding to the LPS and Mg(2+).

deglucoteichoplanin amide compounds are taken up across the outer membranes of E. coli and of P. aeruginos by a Mg(2+):ligand-promoted mechanism, and that the uptake of these compounds across outer membranes is blocked by the presence of 1 mM free Mg(2+).
the polyamine derivatives 766 and 935 of the glycopeptide teicoplanin have a moderate activity against gram-negative bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new antibiotics that can be used to treat infections with P. aeruginosae.
the mechanism of uptake of deglycoteicoplanin aglucoside amide derivatives into Escherichia col and Pseudomonos aeruginosa cells.

developing a new class of antibiotics which can be effective against a wide range of gram-negative bacteria, including P. aeruginose, a major pathogen in cystic fibrosis patients, and which may be used in combination with other agents to combat antibiotic-resistant strains of gram-negative bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deglucosylated teicoplanin derivative 766 is a new, highly active glycopeptide antibiotic with potent activity against P. aeruginosae and E. coli.
both compounds 934 and 766 are able to increase outer membrane permeability by a Mg2+-independent mechanism.
the mechanism of uptake of the deglucoteichlanin amide derivatives MDL 62 766 and 62 934 across the outer membranes of E. coli and Ps. aeruginosa is via a self-promoted uptake process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of the amino group in compound 766, which is not present in compound 934, is responsible for the increased affinity of 766 for LPS.

the mechanism of self-promoted uptake of the deglucoteicolpanin amides across the outer membranes of both E. coli and Ps. aeruginosa is by a process which is dependent on divalent cations, is saturable, and is competitive with the self-promoted entry of other divalent cations.
the polyamine amides of the deglucoteichoplanins, which are inactive as antibiotics against gram-positive bacteria, have been found to possess activity against gram-negative bacteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of a polyamine group to a glycopeptide molecule, in this case to teicoplanin, can increase the activity of this molecule against gram-negative bacteria.

the presence of a dibasic amine at the C63 position is sufficient to allow the teicoplanin backbone to bind to LPS and increase outer membrane permeability, thereby conferring activity on gram-negative bacteria.
deglucoteichoplanin amide compounds are capable of binding to LPS at the Mg(2+ )binding site and permeabilizing the outer membrane.
